name: Chicken Biryani
subtitle: marinated chicken layered under part-cooked rice and sealed for the dum

ingredients.note: on the bone: it holds together and gives the rice flavour

ingredients.qty: a pinch in 4 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Marinate for at least 4 hours. The yogurt needs time to work into bone-in chicken, and this is the difference between a biryani and rice with chicken in it.
Weigh the rice and the water. Biryani is unforgiving of guesswork.

steps.text: Fry the onions slowly in ghee until deep brown and crisp. Drain and reserve.
Marinate the chicken with yogurt, ginger, garlic, chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, half the birista, half the herbs, lemon juice and salt. Refrigerate 4 hours.
Bring the chicken to room temperature for 30 minutes, then spread it in a heavy pot with 3 tbsp ghee and the slit chillies.
Boil the rice in well-salted water with the whole spices until 70 per cent done, then drain immediately.
steps.tip: Drain the second it is ready. Thirty seconds too long and the finished biryani is mush.

steps.text: Layer the rice over the raw chicken and top with the remaining birista, herbs, saffron milk and ghee.
Seal the pot with a tight lid or foil. Cook 6 minutes on high, then 35 minutes on the lowest heat.
steps.tip: Before you rest it, check the thickest piece of chicken reads 74°C / 165°F. If it does not, reseal and give it another 10 minutes on low.

steps.text: Rest 15 minutes before opening, then lift from the bottom so each plate gets rice and chicken.
steps.tip: The rest lets the steam settle. Opening early releases it and the top layer dries.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat covered with a splash of water. Biryani freezes poorly: the rice turns to paste.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
